prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram
Asset type: software engineering research architecture figure, final academic slide and paper illustration.
Style: calm, precise vector-like 2D schematic on pure white, flat pale blue and muted teal fills, slate outlines, minimal amber only for changed or unresolved elements. No gradients, shadows, mascots, decorative circuits, 3D, logos, badges or claims of superior results. Comparable to a carefully typeset conference systems paper. Thin orthogonal arrows with clear arrowheads and ample spacing, no crossing through labels. Large readable black sans-serif text. English labels only, exactly as specified; no extra long text. Use whitespace to keep everything legible when scaled. Wide landscape, 2048x1152. Do not draw charts or invent measurements. Blocks align on a disciplined grid. Each arrow has one clear source and target. Do not draw formal-proof symbols. Use a small restrained title at top.

Title: "Driver Port Factory"
Design three equal vertical panels across the middle, numbered "1 Analysis", "2 Continuous Implementation", "3 Acceptance".
Top input bar: "Complete Linux tree" | "Hollow target kernel" | "Frozen scope and public tests". Arrow down to Analysis.
Analysis contains sequential boxes "Source obligations", "Target route and key premises", "One report + reference index".
Implementation contains "Select one complete work package" then "Read • Code • Integrate • Check" and a small loop labeled "Continue in the same session". Add a concise annotation "A small driver may use one package".
Acceptance contains "Final source + artifact", then "Complete fixed public suite", then "Delivery + evidence". Arrow from final public suite back to Implementation labeled "Concrete failure". Normal arrows run left-to-right from analysis final box to selected package to acceptance.
Below the panels, a wide blue knowledge band: "Task knowledge: original evidence + accepted analysis"; upward thin arrows labeled "Retrieve on demand" to Analysis and Implementation. A downward arrow from analysis report into this band labeled "Retain findings". Small footnote within band: "Report retrieval implemented; unified discovery index pending".
Very bottom gray bar "Controller: versions • progress • execution • receipts". No separate reviewer node. In a corner of Acceptance place "Public coverage ≠ full equivalence".
Keep panel connectors unambiguous; fewer than 18 visual nodes. Show architecture, not measured outcomes.

Accuracy addendum: Keep every original node. Use connected paths, not decorative arrows. The main flow is EXACTLY Input bar -> Source obligations -> Target route and key premises -> One report + reference index -> Select one complete work package -> Read / Code / Integrate / Check -> Final source + artifact -> Complete fixed public suite -> Delivery + evidence. The cross-panel arrow into Select must start at the report, NOT at source obligations. The Candidate arrow into Final source must start at Read/Code/Integrate/Check, NOT at Select. Put the report box near the top of the analysis output side if needed to shorten routing, or use edge ports along column borders. Task knowledge has three connections: report -> knowledge labeled Retain findings; knowledge -> analysis labeled Retrieve on demand; knowledge -> implementation labeled Retrieve on demand. Label the downward knowledge-write arrow Retain findings and the upward knowledge-read arrows Retrieve on demand. Draw acceptance failure -> Read/Code/Integrate/Check. No arrow to the controller foundation strip. Reduce title size and use more whitespace for clean orthogonal paths. Draw all arrowheads at their actual destination. Do not change method detail or omit any node.

Use case: infographic-diagram
Asset type: software engineering research architecture figure, final academic slide and paper illustration.
Style: calm, precise vector-like 2D schematic on pure white, flat pale blue and muted teal fills, slate outlines, minimal amber only for changed or unresolved elements. No gradients, shadows, mascots, decorative circuits, 3D, logos, badges or claims of superior results. Comparable to a carefully typeset conference systems paper. Thin orthogonal arrows with clear arrowheads and ample spacing, no crossing through labels. Large readable black sans-serif text. English labels only, exactly as specified; no extra long text. Use whitespace to keep everything legible when scaled. Wide landscape, 2048x1152. Do not draw charts or invent measurements. Blocks align on a disciplined grid. Each arrow has one clear source and target. Do not draw formal-proof symbols. Use a small restrained title at top.

Title: "Knowledge as an Information-Transfer Mechanism"
Two horizontal lanes separated by generous whitespace.
Upper lane labeled "Within one task". Left column has "Pinned original evidence" and "Accepted analysis". The analysis box includes three short lines "Obligations", "API conditions", "Mapping rationale".
Center has a large pale-blue box "Task knowledge access" with two compartments "Original-source index" and "Accepted-report retrieval". Original evidence goes to the first compartment, analysis goes to the second.
Right has "Implementation / repair worker". Center to worker arrow labeled "Retrieve for the current question".
Above this lane, a separate thin arrow goes from Accepted analysis to the worker via a small box "Required obligations in work packet". It represents mandatory information independent of retrieval.
Below the central box, use a gray DASHED outline box labeled "Planned: unified finding index" connected by a dashed line without suggesting the current system already implements it. A small legend "Dashed box: planned integration".
Lower lane labeled "Across tasks". Left "Selected reusable findings" → middle "Shared library" → right "Next task: pinned read snapshot". Shared library has three rows "Originals", "Observations", "Conditional experience". Arrow from next task snapshot upward to the upper Task knowledge access labeled "Applicable prior knowledge". Do not draw a return arrow from shared updates into the current task snapshot.
Small notes at bottom: "Analysis premises: publish with evidence" and "Implementation lessons: publish after public acceptance". Small final line "Knowledge preserves research; retrieval avoids replaying all research.".
No cylinder implying a single already-unified database. Current access is federated. Arrows show information movement, not proof of semantic truth.

Accuracy addendum: Preserve all original details. Use these exact directed edges: Pinned original evidence -> Original-source index. Accepted analysis -> Accepted-report retrieval. Accepted analysis -> Required obligations in work packet -> Implementation / repair worker. Task knowledge access -> Implementation / repair worker. Selected reusable findings -> Shared library -> Next task: pinned read snapshot -> Task knowledge access. There is NO direct Shared library -> Task knowledge access arrow: the snapshot must mediate it. The snapshot-to-task arrow must run around the right margin and then into the Task knowledge access boundary, avoiding Planned: unified finding index. The work-packet bypass originates from Accepted analysis, never from Pinned original evidence. For clear routing, place Accepted analysis above Pinned original evidence in the left column; every original node remains. Dashed Planned box is separate and only has a dashed connection to task knowledge. No bidirectional arrows. Explicitly follow these endpoints; do not approximate them with panel-level lines.
